prompt: The second `<InfoCard />` was given no content. What did it draw?
hint: Look at the second line of the text of `#app`.

choices.text: An empty `<div class="card">` and a warning
choices.why: A slot with nothing in it is not an error, and this one had text of its own to fall back on.

choices.text: The first card's markup again
choices.why: Each `<InfoCard>` is filled by its own tags; nothing carries from one card to the next.

choices.text: Its fallback, `Nothing to show.`
choices.why: Right. The text written inside `<slot>…</slot>` is drawn when the parent writes nothing.

choices.text: Nothing at all, not even the `<div>`
choices.why: The card's own `<div>` is in its template whatever the parent writes; only the slot's part changes.

prompt: The third card's content reads `typeof secret`, and `secret` is a constant in `InfoCard`'s own script. Why did it print `undefined`?
hint: Where is the content written?

choices.text: `secret` is not a ref, so the template does not see it
choices.why: A plain constant in `<script setup>` is visible to that component's own template; reactivity is not the question here.

choices.text: Slot content sees the parent's scope
choices.why: Right. It is written in `DefaultSlot.vue`, so it sees that file's variables and none of the card's.

choices.text: The slot replaced `secret` with its fallback text
choices.why: The fallback is drawn only when the parent writes nothing; this card was given content.

choices.text: `typeof` runs before the card has mounted
choices.why: Timing has nothing to do with it: the name is looked up in the parent, and the parent has no `secret`.

prompt: A `StatusBadge` comes in three looks: success, warning and error. How should the parent choose one?
hint: The last row of the table.

choices.text: A named slot for each look, filled by the parent
choices.why: Slots carry markup the parent writes; a choice among fixed looks is a value, and three slots would let the parent draw anything in any of them.

choices.text: The default slot, with the look's own markup
choices.why: That hands the parent the freedom to write anything inside the badge, which is the temptation the section warns about.

choices.text: A scoped slot that receives the current look
choices.why: A scoped slot lends values to content the parent writes; here there is nothing for the parent to write.

choices.text: A prop whose value names one of the three looks
choices.why: Right. A few fixed looks are a value, and a prop keeps the badge's markup the badge's own.

prompt: Slot content is compiled in the scope of the ___, the component whose template it is written in.
hint: Not the child that places it.

prompt: What is `#header` on a `<template>` short for?
hint: The same kind of shorthand as `@` for `v-on`.

choices.text: `:header`, binding a prop named `header`
choices.why: `:` is `v-bind`, which passes a value; `#` names the slot the content goes into.

choices.text: `v-slot:header`, which names the slot to fill
choices.why: Right. `#` is to `v-slot` what `@` is to `v-on`.

choices.text: An element id, like `#header` in CSS
choices.why: It looks like a selector, and it is not one: nothing with that id ends up on the page.

choices.text: `name="header"` on the parent's `<template>`
choices.why: `name` is written on the child's `<slot>`; the parent's side is `v-slot`.

prompt: The second `TitledPanel` had no `#footer`. What does the HTML show where the footer would be?
hint: Read the end of the printed HTML.

choices.text: An empty `<footer></footer>`
choices.why: That is what drawing the box anyway would give, and `v-if="$slots.footer"` is there to prevent it.

choices.text: A `<footer>` holding the text `Untitled`
choices.why: `Untitled` is the header slot's fallback; the footer slot has none.

choices.text: The first panel's footer, `75 of 195 minutes done`
choices.why: Each panel is filled by its own tags; the first panel's footer stays in the first panel.

choices.text: The comment `<!--v-if-->`
choices.why: Right. `$slots.footer` was not there, so the `v-if` drew no element and left its placeholder.

prompt: Which of these are true of named slots, as the section shows them? Choose all that apply.
hint: One of them is what happens to a misspelt name.

choices.text: Content outside every `<template #…>` goes to the slot called `default`
choices.why: Right. The paragraph in the first panel went there.

choices.text: The `<template>`s must come in the order the child places them
choices.why: The child's template decides where each slot goes; the parent's order does not matter.

choices.text: A misspelt slot name fills nothing and prints no warning
choices.why: Right. The content does not appear, which is the one silent failure of slots.

choices.text: The `<template>` element itself leaves nothing on the page
choices.why: Right. Only what is inside it is drawn, in the slot it names.

choices.text: Vue warns in the console about a slot name the child does not have
choices.why: It does not, and that silence is why the section says to compare the names first.

prompt: A parent fills `TitledPanel`'s footer with ``. What is drawn at the foot of the panel?
hint: The panel asks `$slots`, and the parent did write a footer.

choices.text: No `<footer>`, as when the parent writes no footer
choices.why: That would hold if the panel looked at what the content rendered; `$slots.footer` only says whether the parent wrote one, and it did.

choices.text: A `<footer>` element with nothing visible in it
choices.why: Right. `$slots.footer` is truthy because the parent wrote the template, so the box is drawn around a `v-if` that came out false.

choices.text: A `<footer>` holding the word `late`
choices.why: `v-if="false"` draws nothing in any slot; the span never reaches the page.

choices.text: The header's fallback, `Untitled`, in the footer
choices.why: A fallback belongs to the slot it is written in; the footer slot has none to draw.

prompt: The first `<SessionTable>` was given no `#row`. What did each of its rows show?
hint: The fallback inside `<slot name="row">`.

choices.text: The course and the minutes
choices.why: That is the parent's `#row` template, which only the second table had.

choices.text: An empty `<li>`
choices.why: The slot has a fallback, so a row with no template still draws something.

choices.text: Its position: `1.`, then `2.`
choices.why: The position is a slot prop; the fallback does not print it.

choices.text: The session's id
choices.why: Right. `s2` and `s5`, the fallback written inside the slot.

prompt: How many slot props does `SessionTable`'s `<slot name="row">` bind?
hint: Count the attributes that start with `:`.

prompt: What can the content inside `<template #row="{ session, position }">` read?
hint: Two sources, and the child decides one of them.

choices.text: Everything in `SessionTable`'s script, now that the slot is scoped
choices.why: A scoped slot opens no door to the child's script: only what the `<slot>` binds is lent.

choices.text: The parent's own variables, plus the two slot props it was lent
choices.why: Right. Nothing else of the child's: the child names exactly what it shares.

choices.text: The slot props, without the parent's variables
choices.why: The content is still written in the parent and still sees the parent's scope; the slot props are added to it.

choices.text: `session` and `position`, plus the `sessions` prop of the child
choices.why: `sessions` is the child's prop and is not bound on the `<slot>`; the parent has its own `sessions`, which is why the name looks reachable.

prompt: Written without destructuring, as `<template #row="props">`, how does the content print the course?
hint: The slot props arrive as one object.

choices.text: `{{ session.course }}`, as before
choices.why: Without the braces nothing is unpacked, so there is no `session` in scope to read.

choices.text: `{{ props[0].course }}`
choices.why: The slot props are an object keyed by name, not a list in the order they were bound.

choices.text: `{{ props.session.course }}`
choices.why: Right. `props` is the whole object, and `session` is one of its keys.

choices.text: `{{ $slots.row.session.course }}`
choices.why: `$slots` is the child's way of asking which slots were filled; the content receives its values through `#row`.

prompt: `WeekPager` starts on 2026-10-19. If a student clicks Next once and then Previous three times, which day of the month does `monday` show?
hint: Each click moves seven days.

prompt: What makes `WeekPager` a renderless component?
hint: Look at its whole template.

choices.text: Its template is its slot and nothing else
choices.why: Right. It holds `monday` and two functions, and every element on the page is the parent's.

choices.text: It has no `<script setup>`, only a template
choices.why: It is the other way round: the script holds the state, and the template holds no markup.

choices.text: Vue skips rendering it until a button is clicked
choices.why: It renders on the first pass like any component; the week was drawn before any click.

choices.text: It returns a function as its children, as React does
choices.why: That is the React render prop; in Vue the parent writes a template and the child passes values to `<slot>`.

prompt: Why does the section expect you to write few renderless components?
hint: What is shared, when the component draws nothing?

choices.text: Vue 3 removed scoped slots on the default slot
choices.why: The demo uses `v-slot` on `WeekPager` itself in Vue 3; nothing was removed.

choices.text: A renderless component re-renders the whole page on each click
choices.why: Only what depends on `monday` changes; the cost is an extra layer, not the rendering.

choices.text: Shared state and logic need no component: a composable does it
choices.why: Right. A function that creates refs and returns them adds no layer to the tree and no template.

choices.text: Scoped slots are slower than props
choices.why: Speed is not the argument; the argument is that a component is the wrong container for logic alone.

prompt: Underneath, what does Vue turn the parent's `#row` template into?
hint: The section says the two models are closer than they look.

choices.text: Static HTML, copied into the child once
choices.why: The rows differ per session, so the content has to run once per item with that item's values.

choices.text: A child component of `SessionTable`
choices.why: No extra component appears; the content stays the parent's and is placed where the `<slot>` is.

choices.text: A prop the parent passes and the child reads
choices.why: Close to React's version, but in Vue the parent writes no prop: the template goes in, and Vue hands it over.

choices.text: A function the child calls with the slot props
choices.why: Right. That is the render prop's shape; what differs is that you write a template, and Vue knows which parts are static.

prompt: The week of 26 October has no sessions, and the panel drew `Nothing here yet.` Why, when `App.vue` wrote a `<ul>` into the default slot?
hint: What did the `<ul>` render?

choices.text: `App.vue` checks the week and passes the text as a prop
choices.why: `App.vue` has no such text any more; the sentence is the panel's own fallback.

choices.text: Its `v-if` came out false, and content like that counts as empty
choices.why: Right. The content rendered only a placeholder comment, so the slot drew its fallback.

choices.text: `$slots.default` was missing, so the panel switched to its fallback
choices.why: The parent did write default content, so `$slots.default` was there; the panel does not ask `$slots` for this slot.

choices.text: The footer's total was zero, and that hides the body
choices.why: The footer and the body are separate slots; the footer was still drawn, with its zero.

prompt: Why did the course cards change from `<h2>` to `<h3>`?
hint: What is the panel's title?

choices.text: `<h3>` is smaller, and the panel needs the room
choices.why: Size is the stylesheet's business; a heading's level says where it sits in the page's outline.

choices.text: Scoped styles in `PlannerPanel` restyle every `<h2>` inside it
choices.why: Scoped styles reach the panel's own elements; the change is about structure, not style.

choices.text: Vue refuses two `<h2>`s in one component
choices.why: Vue checks nothing of the sort; the reason is the reader, not the framework.

choices.text: They sit under the panel's `<h2>`, and headings are a screen reader's map
choices.why: Right. A level that jumps or repeats makes that map wrong.

prompt: In the planner's transcript for the week of 19 October, how many minutes were planned in total?
hint: The footer of the second panel.

prompt: Which of these does `PlannerPanel` have? Choose all that apply.
hint: Read its template, then its props.

choices.text: A title slot, so the parent writes the `<h2>` itself
choices.why: The title is a prop, because it is only text; the panel writes the `<h2>` around it.

choices.text: An `actions` slot beside the title
choices.why: Right. The week's buttons are markup, so they go in a slot.

choices.text: A default slot with a fallback paragraph
choices.why: Right. `Nothing here yet.` is drawn when the body comes out empty.

choices.text: A footer it draws whether or not the parent fills it
choices.why: The `<footer>` has `v-if="$slots.footer"`, so it is drawn only when the parent fills it.

choices.text: A `title` prop that is required
choices.why: Right. `defineProps({ title: { type: String, required: true } })`.

prompt: Match what a component needs from outside to the tool this lesson gives it.
hint: A value, markup, markup per item, or logic with no markup.

pairs.left: a heading with a link in it
how each item of the child's list is drawn
a week and the functions that move it, with no markup

prompt: Put these steps of drawing the second `SessionTable` in the order they happen.
hint: The structure is the child's; the inside of each row is the parent's.
items: The parent passes `sessions` as a prop
Its markup is drawn inside that `<li>`

prompt: A colleague writes `<SessionTable :sessions="sessions"><template #row>{{ session.course }}</template></SessionTable>`. What goes wrong?
hint: Where does the content look `session` up?

choices.text: Nothing: inside `SessionTable` the name `session` exists
choices.why: That is where the loop runs, not where the content is compiled; the content sees the parent's scope.

choices.text: The rows fall back to the id, because `#row` is empty
choices.why: The template is not empty, so the fallback is not drawn; it is the content itself that fails.

choices.text: `session` is not in the parent's scope: the template never received it
choices.why: Right. Without `#row="{ session }"`, the slot props are lent and nobody takes them.

choices.text: Vue refuses `#row` without a value, as a misspelt name
choices.why: A slot with no props named is ordinary; and a misspelt name is the silent case, not a refusal.
